findings.claim: The 'unwrap a Packed kind to its primitive' expression is duplicated verbatim between column_subset and should_encode instead of living in one place.
findings.source: columnstore.py:53 `alias = col.kind.primitive if isinstance(col.kind, Packed) else col.kind` and columnstore.py:63 `kind = col.kind.primitive if isinstance(col.kind, Packed) else col.kind`
findings.remedy: Extract a small `_primitive_kind(col) -> str` helper and call it from both column_subset and should_encode, so the unwrap rule has one owner.

findings.claim: `_MarkerForm` is named as module-private (leading underscore) in markers_native.py, but markers_legacy.py imports it directly to build its own Derived instance -- making it de facto shared cross-module API without any public contract marking that.
findings.remedy: Drop the leading underscore (it's intentionally shared) or add an explicit re-export/`__all__` in markers_native.py that documents _MarkerForm as the intended cross-registry base, so a future edit to markers_native doesn't silently break markers_legacy.

findings.claim: Handle.span changed from a plain, presumably-writable `str` attribute to a read-only property; the compatibility claim in CHANGES.md is explicitly scoped to callers that only read `.span`, and no test in this file exercises assignment to `.span`, so a narrowed write capability is invisible to the passing suite.
findings.source: lifespan.py:70-72 `@property\n    def span(self) -> str:\n        return self._span.value` (no setter); CHANGES.md:9-11 "Every existing caller that only ever read `.span` sees no change"
findings.remedy: Either add a `@span.setter` that does `self._span = Span(value)` for full backward compatibility, or confirm (e.g. via a repo-wide grep) that no caller ever assigns `.span` and record that check as the evidence for this risk boundary.

findings.claim: Span ordering is computed two different ways: `__lt__` rebuilds `list(self.__class__)` on every call, while the module already caches the same list in `SPANS`.
findings.source: lifespan.py:32-33 `order = list(self.__class__)\n        return order.index(self) < order.index(other)` vs. lifespan.py:36 `SPANS = list(Span)`
findings.remedy: Have `__lt__` use the existing `SPANS` list instead of recomputing `list(self.__class__)`, so there's one source of truth for span order.

findings.claim: An empty `actor QuietQueue {}` is added with no caller anywhere in these files and no test referencing it; the comment frames it as speculative scaffolding for a future feature.
findings.source: workspace.swift:57-59 "// Reserved for a future default execution context; not wired into any scoping path yet.\nactor QuietQueue {}"
findings.remedy: Delete QuietQueue now. Add it back when a concrete concurrency/isolation need for Workspace actually shows up -- an unused isolation domain is dead weight and the wrong kind of thing to leave 'for later' since it can be added trivially when actually needed.

findings.claim: CHANGES.md's central claim is that introducing is_driftplane changes no test's skip/run outcome on any platform, but the bundled test suite only calls collect_skips against MAINLAND (where every predicate is false and the check is trivial); GEARSHIFT and TIDELINE skip sets -- the only platforms where is_driftplane's behavior actually matters -- are never asserted.
findings.source: test_platform_guards.py:74-76 `def main() -> int:\n    skipped = collect_skips(MAINLAND, ALL_TESTS)\n    assert skipped == {}, f"mainland should skip nothing, got {skipped}"`
findings.remedy: Add `collect_skips(GEARSHIFT, ALL_TESTS)` and `collect_skips(TIDELINE, ALL_TESTS)` assertions (expected skip-name sets) to main(), so the refactor's own preservation claim is actually checked by the suite rather than only asserted in prose.
